name: Ta Gou Ta Doi 搭九搭对
description: Ta Gou Ta Doi (搭九搭对, 'making nines and pairs') is a Malaysian rummy-like game played with 32 Chinese chess (Xiangqi) pieces used as cards. Each turn: draw one, discard one. Win by collecting three valid sets of two: Gou (two pieces summing to 9) or Doi (pair of same value). Easy and hard variants differ in what counts as a set.
deck: 32 Xiangqi (Chinese chess) pieces used as cards; values 1–8, two colours (red and black).

history.origins: Malaysian game using Xiangqi pieces as playing cards. Name (Fuzhou dialect) means 'making nines and pairs'. Documentation from Alexey Lobashev and Hua Kiong's blog.
timeline: Modern Era: Continues to be played worldwide

setup.deck: 32 Xiangqi pieces mixed face down, arranged in stacks of two in a circle.
setup.dealing: Starting player determined by turning one stack face up and counting by total value. Players take stacks clockwise until each has two stacks; first player takes a third stack, then each takes one piece from next stacks so each has 5 pieces. Pieces held face down in a row.
setup.equipment: Chinese chess (Xiangqi) set of 32 pieces; table.

rules.objective: Collect three valid sets of two pieces and declare to win. Sets are Gou (two pieces whose values sum to 9) or Doi (pair of same value; in hard variant, same colour or the value-2 pair only).
rules.gameplay: Each turn: draw one piece (from discard or from table in distribution order), then discard one. Starting player may declare immediately if holding three sets; otherwise discards. First player to hold three valid sets after drawing declares and wins. If the table is exhausted with no declaration, there is no winner.
keyRules: Draw one, discard one per turn.
Gou: two pieces summing to 9; Doi: pair same value (easy) or identical piece or value-2 pair only (hard).
Win by declaring when holding three valid sets.

strategy.basic: Collect pieces that sum to 9 or pair; discard pieces that do not help form Gou or Doi.
strategy.intermediate: Track which values have been discarded; in easy variant use both Gou and Doi; in hard variant focus on identical pairs or value-2.
strategy.advanced: Optimise draw choice (discard vs table) to complete three sets before opponents; block by taking useful discards.
tips: In easy variant prefer Gou (sum to 9) when you have many high or low pieces; in hard variant only identical pairs or value-2 count.
Track what has been discarded to know which pieces are still in play.

variations.name: Easy
variations.description: Gou: two pieces of any rank and colour whose values add up to 9. Doi: two pieces of the same value, any colour.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Easy variant only changes which pairs count as Doi; no engine overrides needed.

variations.name: Hard
variations.description: Only valid sets are pairs of identical pieces (same colour) or the value-2 pair (marshal and general).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Hard variant only restricts Doi to identical or value-2; no engine overrides needed.

scoring.description: No point scoring; first player to hold three valid sets of two and declare wins. If table is exhausted with no declaration, there is no winner.
scoring.winCondition: First player to hold six pieces forming three valid sets of two (Gou or Doi) and declare wins.

synthesis.shortDescription: Ta Gou Ta Doi is a Malaysian draw-and-discard game for 2–4 players using 32 Xiangqi pieces. Win by declaring when you hold three valid sets of two (Gou: sum to 9, or Doi: pair).
